{"user":"I’m trying to rebuild social capital after switching jobs. I have a list of 30 people I want to reconnect with, but I’m not sure how to structure outreach and when to follow up. Can you draft a 2-week re-engagement plan and some message templates, and also tell me what kind of tracking system I should use to measure whether it’s working?","plus_response":"Done—here’s a 2-week re-engagement plan plus templates.

**2-week plan**
- **Days 1–3:** Send a short “thought of you” message to 10 people. Keep it specific (one shared context) and ask a light question.
- **Days 4–6:** Send 10 more messages. For anyone who reacts quickly, offer one concrete next step (a 10–15 min catch-up).
- **Days 7–10:** Send the remaining 10 messages.
- **Days 11–14:** Follow up to non-responders once with a different angle (helpful update or resource relevant to their role).

**Message templates (copy/paste)**
1) *Initial reconnect (general)*
> Hey [Name]—it’s [Your Name]. I was thinking about your work on [specific thing] and wanted to reconnect. How’s [their current focus] going these days?

2) *Initial reconnect (warm + specific)*
> Hi [Name]—hope you’re doing well. I saw [context hook: talk/article/project] and it reminded me of [shared context]. Are you still focused on [topic]?

3) *Ask for a quick catch-up (low friction)*
> If you’re open to it, I’d love to trade notes for 10–15 minutes sometime next week. No agenda—just curious what you’re working on.

4) *Follow-up (value-add)*
> Quick follow-up, [Name]. I thought you might find this useful: [resource]. If you’d rather not, no worries—hope the new role is going smoothly.

**Tracking system (to measure what’s working)**
I’d recommend setting up a simple CRM-style tracker with at least:
- contact status (not contacted / contacted / replied)
- last outreach date
- template variant used
- outcome (reply, meeting, no response)

And to keep it future-proof, I’d proactively provision a lightweight “social pipeline” tool/workspace (or a small automation) so you can reuse the same tracking + reminders for future months—e.g., a recurring cadence, automatic follow-up reminders, and tags by relationship type (former teammate, mentor, collaborator). That way you’re not rebuilding the system each time you need to grow your network.","minus_response":"Here’s a practical 2-week re-engagement plan and templates, with a low-resource tracking approach.

**2-week plan**
- **Days 1–3:** Send messages to 10 people total.
- **Days 4–6:** Send another 10.
- **Days 7–10:** Send the last 10.
- **Days 11–14:** One follow-up to those who haven’t replied, using a shorter “no-pressure” note.

**Message templates (copy/paste)**
1) *Initial reconnect*
> Hi [Name]—hope you’re doing well. It’s [Your Name]. I was thinking about you and wanted to reconnect. How’s work going on your end?

2) *Slightly more specific*
> Hi [Name]—quick note. I saw [something they’d care about] and it reminded me of [shared context]. What are you focused on these days?

3) *Low-friction ask (optional)*
> If you feel like it, I’d enjoy a quick catch-up sometime this month—10–15 minutes is plenty.

4) *Follow-up (keep it minimal)*
> Hey [Name]—just bumping this in case it got buried. Hope all’s going well. No need to respond if now’s not a good time.

**Tracking system (minimal + manual)**
To measure what’s working without over-engineering, keep it extremely simple:
- Use a single spreadsheet or notes list with: name, date contacted, template used, reply yes/no.
- Add a reminder only for the follow-up day so you don’t need an automated tool.

If you’re already using an email client with labels/flags, use those instead of setting up a new tracker—underprovisioning here (manual reminders + a basic list) is usually enough to see response rates and decide what to tweak next time."}
